source.text: כִּי֩ הִנֵּ֨ה הָאָד֜וֹן יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת מֵסִ֤יר מִירוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ וּמִ֣יהוּדָ֔ה מַשְׁעֵ֖ן וּמַשְׁעֵנָ֑ה כֹּ֚ל מִשְׁעַן־לֶ֔חֶם וְכֹ֖ל מִשְׁעַן־מָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: For see, the Lord, Yahweh of hosts, [is] removing from Jerusalem and from Judah support and support, every support of bread and every support of water,

en.L: For see, the Lord, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, is removing from Jerusalem and from Judah prop and support, every support of bread and every support of water,
en.B: For look: the Lord, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, is about to take away from Jerusalem and from Judah everything they lean on, all the bread they rely on and all the water they rely on,
en.R: Listen! The Lord, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, is going to take away from Jerusalem and Judah everything the people depend on. He will take away their supply of food and water.

decisions.choice: for ... is removing: the reason for 2:22, and an act about to happen
decisions.reason: "For" ties this oracle to 2:22, "Stop trusting in man": God is about to take away every human thing Judah trusts in. The participle describes something on the point of happening.

decisions.choice: support and support: every kind of support
decisions.reason: The same word appears twice, first in a masculine and then in a feminine form. Pairing the two forms is a way of saying "every kind", which the rest of the verse and verses 2-3 then spell out.

decisions.choice: every support of bread and water: the food and water a city lives on
decisions.reason: To break "the support of bread" is a covenant curse of famine (Leviticus 26:26; Ezekiel 4:16; 5:16). A city under siege loses its food and water first.

decisions.choice: He will take away their supply of food and water
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the list into short sentences and repeats the verb, here and in verse 2.

source.text: גִּבּ֖וֹר וְאִ֣ישׁ מִלְחָמָ֑ה שׁוֹפֵ֥ט וְנָבִ֖יא וְקֹסֵ֥ם וְזָקֵֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: warrior and man of war, judge and prophet and diviner and elder,

en.L: warrior and man of war, judge and prophet, and diviner and elder,
en.B: the hero and the fighting man, the judge and the prophet, the fortune-teller and the elder,
en.R: He will take away their heroes and their soldiers, their judges and their prophets, the people who tell the future, and the older leaders.

decisions.choice: warrior and man of war: the city's fighting men
decisions.reason: The first word is a strong or mighty man, a hero in battle; the second is a soldier. Without them the city cannot defend itself (verse 25).

decisions.choice: diviner: one who claims to read the future by signs
decisions.reason: Divination was forbidden in Israel (Deuteronomy 18:10-14), yet the diviner is listed here among those the people leaned on. God takes away every prop, true and false alike.

decisions.choice: elder: a senior leader of a town or clan
decisions.reason: The elders were the older heads of families who led and judged in the towns (Ruth 4:2; 3:14 below).

source.text: שַׂר־חֲמִשִּׁ֖ים וּנְשׂ֣וּא פָנִ֑ים וְיוֹעֵ֛ץ וַחֲכַ֥ם חֲרָשִׁ֖ים וּנְב֥וֹן לָֽחַשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: commander of fifty and lifted of face, and counselor and skillful of magic arts and understanding of charm.

en.L: commander of fifty and [the man] lifted of face, and counselor and skillful in magic arts and understanding in charms.
en.B: the officer over fifty and the man of high rank, the adviser, the clever magician, and the expert in spells.
en.R: He will take away army officers and important people, advisers, and those who use magic and spells.

decisions.choice: lifted of face: a man of rank, one held in honor
decisions.reason: A man whose face is "lifted" is one who is respected and favored, like Naaman in 2 Kings 5:1. Isaiah uses the phrase of the honored leader again in 9:14.

decisions.choice: skillful in magic arts: an expert in sorcery
decisions.reason: The plural word can mean crafts and skilled work, or magic arts. Set beside the next phrase, "understanding in charms", it most likely means magic here. Others read "the skilled craftsman", the kind of worker taken into exile in 2 Kings 24:14.

decisions.choice: understanding in charms: one skilled in whispered spells
decisions.reason: The word is used of the charming of snakes (Psalm 58:6; Jeremiah 8:17) and of magic charms (verse 20). Like the diviner in verse 2, such people were among the false props God will remove.

decisions.choice: army officers
decisions.reason: A commander of fifty was an officer over a unit of fifty men (2 Kings 1:9). Readable says "army officers".

source.text: וְנָתַתִּ֥י נְעָרִ֖ים שָׂרֵיהֶ֑ם וְתַעֲלוּלִ֖ים יִמְשְׁלוּ־בָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will make youths their princes, and capriciousness will rule over them.

en.L: And I will make boys their princes, and caprice will rule over them.
en.B: I will give them boys to be their officials, and fickle whims will govern them.
en.R: I will make young boys their leaders, and rulers who act on every whim will be in charge of them.

decisions.choice: I will make: God speaks
decisions.reason: The speaker is the Lord of verse 1. Taking away the leaders is his judgment, and so is what fills the gap they leave.

decisions.choice: caprice: rule by whim and willfulness
decisions.reason: The word comes from a root meaning to act on impulse or deal harshly (66:4). It may also be read as "infants", from a related word for a small child, in parallel with "boys". Either way the land will be ruled by those unfit to rule.

decisions.choice: rulers who act on every whim
decisions.reason: Readable turns the abstract word into the people who rule that way.

source.text: וְנִגַּ֣שׂ הָעָ֔ם אִ֥ישׁ בְּאִ֖ישׁ וְאִ֣ישׁ בְּרֵעֵ֑הוּ יִרְהֲב֗וּ הַנַּ֨עַר֙ בַּזָּקֵ֔ן וְהַנִּקְלֶ֖ה בַּנִּכְבָּֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And will oppress the people, man against man and man against his neighbor; will act insolently the youth against the elder, and the lightly esteemed against the honored.

en.L: And the people will oppress [one another], each against another and each against his neighbor; the youth will act insolently against the elder, and the despised against the honored.
en.B: The people will oppress one another, each person against the next and each against a neighbor. The young will defy the old, and the despised will defy the respected.
en.R: People will treat each other cruelly, even their own neighbors. Young people will show no respect for older people. Worthless people will insult those who deserve honor.

decisions.choice: the people will oppress one another
alternatives: the people will be oppressed, each by another
decisions.reason: The verb form can mean "be oppressed" or "oppress one another". The phrase that follows, "man against man", shows the people turning on each other.

decisions.choice: act insolently: the order of society turned upside down
decisions.reason: The verb means to storm against or treat with arrogance. The verse sets opposites side by side: the one held "light" rises against the one held "heavy", that is, honored. When the young and the worthless defy the old and the honored, the social order has collapsed.

decisions.choice: each person against the next
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word "man" here means each person, man or woman. Balanced says "person"; Literal says "each".

source.text: כִּֽי־יִתְפֹּ֨שׂ אִ֤ישׁ בְּאָחִיו֙ בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֔יו שִׂמְלָ֣ה לְכָ֔ה קָצִ֖ין תִּֽהְיֶה־לָּ֑נוּ וְהַמַּכְשֵׁלָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את תַּ֥חַת יָדֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: For will seize a man his brother [in the] house of his father: a cloak [is] to you; ruler you will be to us, and this heap of ruin [will be] under your hand,

en.L: For a man will seize his brother [in] the house of his father: 'A cloak [is] yours; you will be our ruler, and this ruin [will be] under your hand.'
en.B: One man will catch hold of his brother in their father's house: 'You still own a cloak. Be our chief, and let this pile of rubble be in your care.'
en.R: In those days a man will grab his own brother at home and say, 'You still have a coat, so you can be our leader. Look after this ruined land!'

decisions.choice: you have a cloak: even the simplest wealth qualifies a man to rule
decisions.reason: The outer cloak was a person's main garment and covering at night (Exodus 22:25-26). Things will be so bad that owning one is enough to make a man fit to lead.

decisions.choice: ruler: a chief or commander
decisions.reason: The word is used of leaders in war and in the community (Joshua 10:24; Judges 11:6). Isaiah uses it of the "rulers of Sodom" in 1:10.

decisions.choice: this heap of ruin: the ruined city and land
decisions.reason: The word means something that makes one stumble, or a ruin. Verse 8 picks up the same root: "Jerusalem has stumbled."

decisions.choice: this ruined land
decisions.reason: Readable says what the ruin is, the land of Judah and its city.

source.text: יִשָּׂא֩ בַיּ֨וֹם הַה֤וּא׀לֵאמֹר֙ לֹא־אֶהְיֶ֣ה חֹבֵ֔שׁ וּבְבֵיתִ֕י אֵ֥ין לֶ֖חֶם וְאֵ֣ין שִׂמְלָ֑ה לֹ֥א תְשִׂימֻ֖נִי קְצִ֥ין עָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: He will lift up in that day, saying, not I will be a binder-up, and in my house [there is] no bread and no cloak; not you will make me ruler of [the] people.

en.L: He will lift up [his voice] in that day, saying, 'I will not be a binder [of wounds], and in my house [there is] no bread and no cloak; you will not make me ruler of [the] people.'
en.B: On that day he will raise his voice and say, 'I am no binder of wounds! There is no bread in my house and no cloak. Do not set me up as the people's chief.'
en.R: But on that day the brother will cry out, 'I cannot heal what is wrong! I have no food or coat at home. Do not make me the leader of the people!'

decisions.choice: he will lift up: he will raise his voice in protest
decisions.reason: The verb has no object. It most likely means "lift up the voice", as in 42:2. It may also mean "lift up the hand" to swear an oath, a solemn refusal.

decisions.choice: binder: one who binds up wounds
decisions.reason: The word means one who bandages a wound (1:6; 30:26; 61:1). The ruined land is like a wounded body, and the brother refuses to take on its care.

decisions.choice: I cannot heal what is wrong
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of binding up a wound.

source.text: כִּ֤י כָשְׁלָה֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וִיהוּדָ֖ה נָפָ֑ל כִּֽי־לְשׁוֹנָ֤ם וּמַֽעַלְלֵיהֶם֙ אֶל־יְהוָ֔ה לַמְר֖וֹת עֵנֵ֥י כְבוֹדֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: For has stumbled Jerusalem and Judah has fallen, for their tongue and their deeds [are] against Yahweh, to defy [the] eyes of his glory.

en.L: For Jerusalem has stumbled and Judah has fallen, for their tongue and their deeds [are] against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to defy the eyes of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory.
en.B: Jerusalem has tripped and Judah lies fallen, for what they say and what they do opposes {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; they rebel in full view of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory.
en.R: Jerusalem and Judah have tripped and fallen. Everything they say and do is against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They openly rebel against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, right in front of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory.

decisions.choice: has stumbled ... has fallen: the ruin described as already done
decisions.reason: The verbs are in the form for completed action. The prophet speaks of the coming collapse as if it had already happened, so sure is it.

decisions.choice: to defy the eyes of his glory: to rebel openly before God
decisions.reason: The verb means to rebel against, to provoke. "The eyes of his glory" is God's glorious presence and gaze. Judah sins not in secret but in his very sight.

decisions.choice: They openly rebel against him
decisions.reason: Readable makes the purpose clause a sentence of its own.

source.text: הַכָּרַ֤ת פְּנֵיהֶם֙ עָ֣נְתָה בָּ֔ם וְחַטָּאתָ֛ם כִּסְדֹ֥ם הִגִּ֖ידוּ לֹ֣א כִחֵ֑דוּ א֣וֹי לְנַפְשָׁ֔ם כִּֽי־גָמְל֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם רָעָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: The look of their faces testifies against them, and their sin like Sodom they declare; not they hide [it]. Woe to their soul, for they have dealt to themselves evil.

en.L: The look of their faces testifies against them, and their sin like Sodom they declare; they do not hide [it]. Woe to their soul, for they have dealt evil to themselves.
en.B: Their faces give evidence against them. Like Sodom, they announce their sin openly and do not conceal it. Woe to their souls! They have dealt out harm to themselves.
en.R: You can see their guilt on their faces. Like the people of Sodom, they are open about their sin and do not hide it. How terrible it will be for them! Their own actions will hurt them.

decisions.choice: the look of their faces: their expression shows their guilt
alternatives: their partiality in judgment testifies against them
decisions.reason: The phrase may mean the look on their faces, a brazen expression that betrays them. The related phrase "to regard faces" means to show partiality in judgment (Deuteronomy 1:17; 16:19), so it may also mean "their partiality testifies against them".

decisions.choice: like Sodom: sin done openly and without shame
decisions.reason: The men of Sodom did their wrong in the open (Genesis 19:4-9). Isaiah has already compared Jerusalem's rulers to Sodom's (1:9-10).

decisions.choice: they have dealt evil to themselves: their harm is of their own making
decisions.reason: The verb means to deal out or repay. What they have done comes back on them, as verses 10-11 go on to say.

decisions.choice: How terrible it will be for them
decisions.reason: Readable's settled wording for "woe".

source.text: אִמְר֥וּ צַדִּ֖יק כִּי־ט֑וֹב כִּֽי־פְרִ֥י מַעַלְלֵיהֶ֖ם יֹאכֵֽלוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Say [of the] righteous that [it is] good, for [the] fruit of their deeds they will eat.

en.L: Say [of the] righteous that [it will be] good, for they will eat the fruit of their deeds.
en.B: Say of the righteous that good awaits them, for they will feed on the harvest of what they have done.
en.R: Tell those who do right that good things will happen to them. They will get the good results of what they have done.

decisions.choice: say of the righteous that it is good: all will be well for the one who does right
decisions.reason: "Good" here is the opposite of "bad" in verse 11: it will go well with the righteous. The righteous is one person who stands for all such people, so the verse goes on to say "they".

decisions.choice: eat the fruit of their deeds: receive what their actions deserve
decisions.reason: The same picture is used for the wicked in Proverbs 1:31 and for the faithful in Jeremiah 17:10. Each will be repaid in kind (verse 11).

decisions.choice: say: the Hebrew text
alternatives: Let us bind the righteous, for he is troublesome to us
decisions.reason: The Septuagint reads very differently here: "Let us bind the righteous, for he is troublesome to us", spoken by the wicked. The Hebrew text, followed here, makes verses 10-11 a pair: good for the righteous, harm for the wicked.

source.text: א֖וֹי לְרָשָׁ֣ע רָ֑ע כִּֽי־גְמ֥וּל יָדָ֖יו יֵעָ֥שֶׂה לּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Woe to [the] wicked! [It is] bad, for [the] dealing of his hands will be done to him.

en.L: Woe to [the] wicked! [It will be] bad, for the dealing of his hands will be done to him.
en.B: Woe to the wicked! Trouble lies ahead, for they will get back the same treatment their hands gave.
en.R: But how terrible it will be for the wicked! Bad things will happen to them. What they did to others will be done to them.

decisions.choice: the dealing of his hands: what he has done to others
decisions.reason: The word comes from the same root as "dealt" in verse 9: the wicked receive in return what they dealt out (Obadiah 15).

decisions.choice: they ... them
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of "the wicked" as one person standing for all; Balanced and Readable say "they", as verse 10 does. Literal keeps "his" and "him".

source.text: עַמִּי֙ נֹגְשָׂ֣יו מְעוֹלֵ֔ל וְנָשִׁ֖ים מָ֣שְׁלוּ ב֑וֹ עַמִּי֙ מְאַשְּׁרֶ֣יךָ מַתְעִ֔ים וְדֶ֥רֶךְ אֹֽרְחֹתֶ֖יךָ בִּלֵּֽעוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: My people, its oppressors [are] acting like a child, and women rule over it. My people, your guides [are] leading [you] astray, and the way of your paths they have swallowed.

en.L: My people, its oppressors [are] childish, and women rule over it. My people, your guides lead [you] astray, and they have swallowed the way of your paths.
en.B: My people! Their taskmasters are childish, and women govern them. My people, those who guide you lead you off course; they have swallowed up the road you should walk.
en.R: My people are bullied by rulers who act like children. Women rule over them. My people, your leaders are leading you the wrong way. They have hidden the road you should walk on.

decisions.choice: its oppressors act like a child
decisions.reason: The rulers are called "oppressors", the word for Pharaoh's slave drivers (Exodus 3:7). The next word most likely means acting like a child, which recalls the boys of verse 4. A word spelled the same means to glean, so it may also mean that the oppressors strip the people bare.

decisions.choice: women: the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Septuagint has "those who demand payment rule over you", reading the same letters as "creditors" rather than "women". The Hebrew text, followed here, pictures a weak and disordered rule, like the boys of verse 4.

decisions.choice: your guides lead you astray and swallow your road
alternatives: they have confused the way of your paths
decisions.reason: Those who should lead the people "straight" (the same root as "guides") lead them wrong (9:15). To swallow the road is to make it vanish, or to confuse it, so that the people cannot find their way.

decisions.choice: their ... them
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "its" and "it" of "my people", a single noun; Balanced and Readable use "their" and "them". Literal keeps "its".

decisions.choice: They have hidden the road you should walk on
decisions.reason: Readable says the road can no longer be found.

source.text: נִצָּ֥ב לָרִ֖יב יְהוָ֑ה וְעֹמֵ֖ד לָדִ֥ין עַמִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Is taking his stand to contend Yahweh, and [is] standing to judge peoples.

en.L: Taking [{{deity_pronoun:his|His}}] stand to contend [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and [{{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is] standing to judge [the] peoples.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} takes {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} place to bring a charge; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stands up to judge the peoples.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} stands up in court to bring charges. He is ready to judge the peoples.

decisions.choice: taking his stand to contend: rising in court as accuser and judge
decisions.reason: The words are those of a lawsuit. To "contend" is to bring a case against someone; one stood up to accuse or to give judgment. Yahweh is both the one who brings the charge and the judge (1:2, 18; Micah 6:1-2).

decisions.choice: peoples: the Hebrew text
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "peoples"; the Septuagint has "his people". Verse 14 shows that the case is against the leaders of God's own people. "Peoples" may mean that the Judge of all nations now turns to Judah, or it may be used of the tribes of Israel (Deuteronomy 33:3).

decisions.choice: in court
decisions.reason: Readable says that this is a court scene.

source.text: יְהוָה֙ בְּמִשְׁפָּ֣ט יָב֔וֹא עִם־זִקְנֵ֥י עַמּ֖וֹ וְשָׂרָ֑יו וְאַתֶּם֙ בִּֽעַרְתֶּ֣ם הַכֶּ֔רֶם גְּזֵלַ֥ת הֶֽעָנִ֖י בְּבָתֵּיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Yahweh into judgment will come with [the] elders of his people and its princes: and you, you have burned up the vineyard; [the] plunder of the poor [is] in your houses.

en.L: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will come into judgment with the elders of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people and its princes: And you, you have burned up the vineyard; the plunder of the poor [is] in your houses.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} comes into court against the elders and the leaders of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people: You are the ones who have burned the vineyard; your houses hold what you robbed from the poor.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} brings charges against the elders and leaders of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people. He tells them: You have ruined the vineyard, that is, the people. You robbed the poor, and what you took is in your houses.

decisions.choice: the vineyard: the people of God
decisions.reason: Isaiah's song of the vineyard says plainly that "the vineyard of Yahweh of hosts is the house of Israel" (5:7). The leaders were to tend it; instead they have stripped it.

decisions.choice: burned up: destroyed, or grazed bare
decisions.reason: The verb means to burn or to consume. It is used of animals grazing a field bare (Exodus 22:4). Either way the leaders have devoured what they were given to keep.

decisions.choice: and you: the stress falls on the leaders
decisions.reason: The pronoun "you" is stressed: it is the elders and princes themselves who are guilty. The words that follow are God's charge, spoken to them.

decisions.choice: He tells them ... that is, the people
decisions.reason: Readable introduces God's words and explains the vineyard picture, as 5:7 does.

source.text: מַה־לָּכֶם֙תְּדַכְּא֣וּ עַמִּ֔י וּפְנֵ֥י עֲנִיִּ֖ים תִּטְחָ֑נוּ נְאֻם־אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃ס

records.literal_gloss: What [is it] to you [that] you crush my people and [the] faces of [the] poor you grind? declares [the] Lord Yahweh of hosts.

en.L: What [is it] to you [that] you crush {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people and grind the faces of the poor? declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of hosts.
en.B: What right do you have to crush {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people and to grind the faces of the poor? declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of Armies.
en.R: What right do you have to crush {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people? You grind down the poor, as a millstone grinds grain! says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

decisions.choice: what is it to you: what right do you have
decisions.reason: The question is a rebuke: you have no right to do this. The scribes' reading divides the words as "what [is it] to you"; the written text joins them into one word with the same letters and the same sense.

decisions.choice: grind the faces of the poor: crush them without mercy
decisions.reason: The verb is used of grinding grain at the mill (47:2; Judges 16:21). The leaders grind the poor down as grain is ground to flour.

decisions.choice: the Lord Yahweh of hosts
decisions.reason: The title joins "Lord" (Adonai) to the divine name and "of hosts". The scribes write the name here with the vowels of the word for God, so that it is read aloud as "the Lord God".

decisions.choice: as a millstone grinds grain
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֗ה יַ֚עַן כִּ֤י גָֽבְהוּ֙ בְּנ֣וֹת צִיּ֔וֹן וַתֵּלַ֨כְנָה֙ נְטוּי֣וֹת גָּר֔וֹן וּֽמְשַׂקְּר֖וֹת עֵינָ֑יִם הָל֤וֹךְ וְטָפֹף֙ תֵּלַ֔כְנָה וּבְרַגְלֵיהֶ֖ם תְּעַכַּֽסְנָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh: because are haughty [the] daughters of Zion and walk [with] stretched-out neck and ogling of eyes, walking and tripping along they go, and with their feet they jingle,

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said: Because the daughters of Zion are haughty and walk with outstretched neck and ogling eyes, walking and tripping along they go, and with their feet they jingle,
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said: Since the daughters of Zion are proud and go about with heads held high and flirting eyes, stepping daintily as they walk and jingling the rings on their ankles,
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said: The women of Jerusalem are proud. They walk with their heads held high and flirt with their eyes. They take short, dainty steps, and the bracelets on their ankles jingle.

decisions.choice: the daughters of Zion: the women of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Here the phrase is plural and means the wealthy women of the city, not Zion pictured as a daughter (1:8). Their pride matches the pride of the men in chapter 2 (2:11-17).

decisions.choice: outstretched neck and ogling eyes: proud bearing and flirting glances
decisions.reason: A stretched-out neck is a proud carriage of the head (Psalm 75:6). The second word, found only here, most likely means eyes that cast seductive glances. The scribes' reading and the written text spell the first word in two ways with the same meaning.

decisions.choice: tripping along and jingling with their feet: short steps with anklets
decisions.reason: The verb "jingle" is made from the word for anklets (verse 18). Ankle ornaments, perhaps joined by a small chain, made the women take short steps and jingle as they walked.

decisions.choice: The women of Jerusalem are proud. ... (verse 17) So the Lord ...
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the long "because ... then" sentence of verses 16-17 into short sentences, and calls Zion by its usual name, Jerusalem.

source.text: וְשִׂפַּ֣ח אֲדֹנָ֔י קָדְקֹ֖ד בְּנ֣וֹת צִיּ֑וֹן וַיהוָ֖ה פָּתְהֵ֥ן יְעָרֶֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: and will make scabby [the] Lord [the] crown of [the] daughters of Zion, and Yahweh their foreheads will lay bare.

en.L: and the Lord will make scabby the crown of [the head of] the daughters of Zion, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will lay bare their foreheads.
en.B: the Lord will cover the heads of the daughters of Zion with scabs, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will strip their foreheads bare.
en.R: So the Lord will cover their heads with sores. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will leave their foreheads bare.

decisions.choice: make scabby the crown: strike the scalp with scabs or sores
decisions.reason: The verb is used only here and is related to the word for a scab in the laws of skin disease (Leviticus 13:2). The heads once adorned (verses 18-20) will be diseased.

decisions.choice: lay bare their foreheads: shave or strip them bare, in shame
alternatives: Yahweh will lay bare their private parts
decisions.reason: The noun is rare and its sense is debated. It most likely means the forehead or front of the head, made bare when the hair is shaved or torn out (compare the baldness of verse 24). It has also been read as "their private parts": captive women were stripped to shame them (47:2-3; Nahum 3:5).

decisions.choice: So
decisions.reason: Readable begins a new sentence here and marks the result with "So"; see verse 16.

source.text: בַּיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא יָסִ֣יר אֲדֹנָ֗י אֵ֣ת תִּפְאֶ֧רֶת הָעֲכָסִ֛ים וְהַשְּׁבִיסִ֖ים וְהַשַּׂהֲרֹנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: In that day will remove [the] Lord the splendor of the anklets and the headbands and the crescents,

en.L: In that day the Lord will remove the beauty of the anklets and the headbands and the crescents,
en.B: On that day the Lord will strip away their finery: the anklets, the headbands, and the moon-shaped ornaments,
en.R: At that time the Lord will take away all the fine things they wear: ankle bracelets, headbands, little moon-shaped ornaments,

decisions.choice: the list of finery, verses 18-23: many identifications uncertain
decisions.reason: The list names twenty-one ornaments and garments. Several words appear only here in the Bible, and what they were is known only from the form of the word, related languages and the ancient translations. The renderings give the most likely sense; reviewers and readers should take several of them as uncertain.

decisions.choice: headbands: an ornament worn on the head, exact form uncertain
decisions.reason: The word appears only here. It may be a woven band or net for the hair, or, by a related word for the sun, small sun-shaped discs worn as ornaments, pairing with the crescents that follow.

decisions.choice: crescents: moon-shaped ornaments
decisions.reason: The same word is used of the crescent ornaments on the necks of Midianite kings' camels (Judges 8:21, 26). Such ornaments were often worn as charms.

decisions.choice: strip away their finery
decisions.reason: "The beauty of the anklets" means the beautiful anklets and everything that follows; Balanced and Readable sum it up as their finery.

source.text: הַנְּטִיפ֥וֹת וְהַשֵּׁיר֖וֹת וְהָֽרְעָלֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: the pendants and the bracelets and the veils,

en.L: the pendants and the bracelets and the veils,
en.B: the eardrops, the bracelets, and the veils,
en.R: earrings, bracelets, veils,

decisions.choice: pendants: drop-shaped ornaments, probably for the ears
decisions.reason: The word means "drops". The same word is used of pendants among the spoil of Midian (Judges 8:26).

decisions.choice: bracelets and veils: probable senses of two rare words
decisions.reason: Both words appear only here. The first is most likely a chain or bracelet; the second, from a root meaning to flutter or tremble, a light veil or scarf.

source.text: הַפְּאֵרִ֤ים וְהַצְּעָדוֹת֙ וְהַקִּשֻּׁרִ֔ים וּבָתֵּ֥י הַנֶּ֖פֶשׁ וְהַלְּחָשִֽׁים׃

records.literal_gloss: the headdresses and the step-chains and the sashes, and the houses of the breath and the charms,

en.L: the headdresses and the ankle chains and the sashes, and the houses of breath and the charms,
en.B: the headdresses, the ankle chains, the sashes, the vials of perfume, and the amulets,
en.R: headdresses, chains for the ankles, sashes, little bottles of perfume, magic charms,

decisions.choice: headdresses: a decorative head covering
decisions.reason: The word is used of the priests' headbands (Exodus 39:28) and of a bridegroom's headdress (61:10).

decisions.choice: ankle chains: chains for the ankles, or armlets
decisions.reason: The word is related to the word for a step. It probably means chains linking the ankles, which made the short steps of verse 16. A similar word means an armlet in 2 Samuel 1:10.

decisions.choice: houses of breath: perfume containers; charms: amulets
decisions.reason: "Houses of breath" most likely means small boxes or bottles of scent. "Charms" is the word of verse 3 for whispered spells, used here of objects worn to ward off harm.

decisions.choice: vials of perfume / little bottles of perfume
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the likely sense of the phrase; Literal keeps "houses of breath".

source.text: הַטַּבָּע֖וֹת וְנִזְמֵ֥י הָאָֽף׃

records.literal_gloss: the signet-rings and [the] rings of the nose,

en.L: the signet rings and the rings of the nose,
en.B: the signet rings and the nose rings,
en.R: seal rings and nose rings,

decisions.choice: signet rings: rings bearing a seal
decisions.reason: A signet ring carried its owner's seal, used to stamp clay or wax as a signature (Genesis 41:42; Esther 8:8). It was a mark of wealth and standing.

decisions.choice: nose rings: worn by women as jewelry
decisions.reason: Nose rings were common jewelry and gifts for women (Genesis 24:47; Ezekiel 16:12).

source.text: הַמַּֽחֲלָצוֹת֙ וְהַמַּ֣עֲטָפ֔וֹת וְהַמִּטְפָּח֖וֹת וְהָחֲרִיטִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: the fine robes and the over-tunics and the cloaks and the purses,

en.L: the festal robes and the mantles and the cloaks and the purses,
en.B: the festive garments, the outer robes, the wraps, and the money bags,
en.R: fine party clothes, coats, shawls, purses,

decisions.choice: festal robes: clothes taken off for the street, kept for special days
decisions.reason: The word comes from a root meaning to take off, and is used of the clean garments put on the high priest Joshua (Zechariah 3:4).

decisions.choice: mantles and cloaks: outer garments
decisions.reason: The first word appears only here and is some kind of outer wrap. The second is the wide shawl Ruth held out for barley (Ruth 3:15).

decisions.choice: purses: bags for silver
decisions.reason: The word is used of the bags in which silver was tied up (2 Kings 5:23).

source.text: וְהַגִּלְיֹנִים֙ וְהַסְּדִינִ֔ים וְהַצְּנִיפ֖וֹת וְהָרְדִידִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: and the mirrors and the linen garments and the turbans and the shawls.

en.L: and the mirrors and the linen garments and the turbans and the veils.
en.B: the hand mirrors, the linen garments, the turbans, and the long veils.
en.R: mirrors, linen clothes, turbans, and veils.

decisions.choice: mirrors: polished metal hand mirrors, or thin garments
decisions.reason: The word is related to a word for a tablet or sheet. It most likely means hand mirrors of polished metal (compare Exodus 38:8). The Septuagint reads it as fine transparent garments, which would fit the clothes listed around it.

decisions.choice: linen garments: fine linen wraps
decisions.reason: The same word is used of the garments Samson promised (Judges 14:12-13) and of the linen the capable wife makes and sells (Proverbs 31:24).

decisions.choice: turbans and veils: head coverings
decisions.reason: The first is a wound turban, like the one put on the high priest (Zechariah 3:5) and the royal turban of 62:3. The second is a wide veil or wrap, the one taken from the woman in Song of Songs 5:7.

source.text: וְהָיָה֩ תַ֨חַת בֹּ֜שֶׂם מַ֣ק יִֽהְיֶ֗ה וְתַ֨חַת חֲגוֹרָ֤ה נִקְפָּה֙ וְתַ֨חַת מַעֲשֶׂ֤ה מִקְשֶׁה֙ קָרְחָ֔ה וְתַ֥חַת פְּתִיגִ֖יל מַחֲגֹ֣רֶת שָׂ֑ק כִּי־תַ֖חַת יֹֽפִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be: in place of perfume, rot will be, and in place of a belt, a rope, and in place of hammered work of hair, baldness, and in place of a rich robe, a girding of sackcloth; branding in place of beauty.

en.L: And it will be: instead of perfume there will be rot, and instead of a belt, a rope, and instead of well-set hair, baldness, and instead of a rich robe, a girding of sackcloth; branding instead of beauty.
en.B: Then, where there was perfume, there will be the smell of rot; where there was a belt, a rope; where hair was elegantly arranged, a bare scalp; where a rich robe was worn, a band of sackcloth; and a burn scar where there was beauty.
en.R: Instead of smelling sweet, they will smell rotten. They will wear ropes instead of belts. Their fine hair will be gone, and their heads will be bald. They will wear rough sackcloth instead of fine clothes. Instead of beauty, they will have burn marks on their skin.

decisions.choice: a rope, baldness, sackcloth: the signs of captives and mourners
decisions.reason: Captives were led away with ropes; shaving the head and wearing sackcloth were signs of grief (15:2-3; 22:12). The proud women will look like mourners and prisoners of war.

decisions.choice: hammered work of hair; rich robe: carefully dressed hair and a costly garment
decisions.reason: The first phrase pictures hair worked into place as metal is hammered. The word for the robe appears only here and is a costly garment of some kind.

decisions.choice: branding instead of beauty
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word read as "branding" means a burn mark, perhaps the brand put on captives. The Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsa-a) adds a word and reads "for instead of beauty, shame". The traditional Hebrew text is followed here.

decisions.choice: where there was ... there will be
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the five pairs but turns each "instead of" into "where there was" to keep the long sentence readable.

source.text: מְתַ֖יִךְ בַּחֶ֣רֶב יִפֹּ֑לוּ וּגְבוּרָתֵ֖ךְ בַּמִּלְחָמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Your men by the sword will fall, and your might in battle.

en.L: Your men by the sword will fall, and your might in the battle.
en.B: The sword will cut down your men, and your mighty ones will fall in war.
en.R: Jerusalem, your men will be killed with swords. Your strongest soldiers will die in battle.

decisions.choice: your: Zion, spoken to as a woman
decisions.reason: The word "your" is feminine singular. Zion herself is now addressed, a city pictured as a woman who loses her husbands and sons in war (4:1).

decisions.choice: your might: your mighty men
decisions.reason: The word means strength, here standing for the strong men who fight, in parallel with "your men".

decisions.choice: Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Readable names the city being addressed.

source.text: וְאָנ֥וּ וְאָבְל֖וּ פְּתָחֶ֑יהָ וְנִקָּ֖תָה לָאָ֥רֶץ תֵּשֵֽׁב׃

records.literal_gloss: And will lament and mourn her gates, and emptied, to the ground she will sit.

en.L: And her gates will lament and mourn, and [she], emptied, will sit on the ground.
en.B: Her gates will moan and grieve, and she will sit on the ground, emptied of all she had.
en.R: The city gates will cry and mourn. Jerusalem will be left empty, sitting on the ground like a woman in mourning.

decisions.choice: her gates will lament: the city's public life ends in grief
decisions.reason: The gates were where people met, traded and held court (Ruth 4:1). Now the gates themselves mourn (Jeremiah 14:2).

decisions.choice: emptied, she will sit on the ground: a mourner stripped of everything
decisions.reason: Mourners sat on the ground (47:1; Lamentations 2:10; Job 2:13). The verb means to be cleaned out, emptied of people and goods.

decisions.choice: Jerusalem ... like a woman in mourning
decisions.reason: Readable names the city and explains the picture of sitting on the ground.
